Class ConnectionAcceptor

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsoft.mesos.server.network.tcp.ConnectionAcceptor
All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable
public class ConnectionAcceptor extends Object implements Runnable
Accepts TCP client connections for the server.

This class is the TCP bootstrap point of the server-side network layer. It owns the listening ServerSocket, accepts raw client sockets, and creates one VirtualViewTCP for each accepted connection.

The acceptor does not parse client messages and does not execute application commands. After a socket is accepted, the corresponding virtual view becomes responsible for reading the TCP stream, registering the session through the ServerConnectionLifecycle, and routing client payloads through the shared MessageRouter.

  • Constructor Details

    • ConnectionAcceptor

      public ConnectionAcceptor(int port, ServerConnectionLifecycle serverConnectionLifecycle, MessageRouter router)
      Creates a TCP acceptor configured for one listening port.
      Parameters:
      port - TCP port to bind; 0 lets the operating system choose an available port
      serverConnectionLifecycle - connection manager used by created virtual views to register sessions
      router - router used by created virtual views to dispatch client payloads to the correct server phase
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if port is outside the valid TCP port range
      NullPointerException - if serverConnectionLifecycle or router is null

  • Method Details

    • start

      public void start() throws IOException
      Opens the listening server socket.

      This method prepares the acceptor for run(). It must be called before the accept loop starts. If the configured port is 0, the actual chosen port can be read with getPort() after this method returns.

      Throws:
      IOException - if the server socket cannot be opened
      IllegalStateException - if the acceptor is already running

    • run

      public void run()
      Runs the TCP accept loop.

      Each accepted socket is wrapped in a new VirtualViewTCP. The virtual view is then started on its own thread, so each connected client has an independent TCP reader and writer boundary.

      Specified by:
      run in interface Runnable
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if start() was not called before running the accept loop, or if accepting a connection fails while the acceptor is active

    • getPort

      public int getPort()
      Returns the TCP port used by this acceptor.

      Before start(), this is the configured port. After the server socket is opened, this is the actual local port bound by the operating system.

      Returns:
      configured or bound TCP port
